title: ר' אליעזר הגדול

paragraphs: (b) He is the unqualified Rabbi Eliezer (Halikhot Olam). Rashi writes unqualified R.A. is ben Shammua (see there). Tosafot, Keritot 18a: above read Rabbi Elazar, here Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yehoshua’s disputant. Likewise Tosafot, Bava Kamma 78, end of a; Bava Batra 156a; Techillat Chokhmah, rule 41, 116b; and Birkat Hazevach, Zevachim, chapter 11, 93a: there were two Rabbi Eliezers, implying both with yod. This is difficult: Tosafot, Bava Kamma 16b and Sanhedrin 16b, write one with yod, Rabbi Eliezer, and one Rabbi Elazar. Tosafot Yom Tov, Temurah, chapter 3, mishnah 3, where Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Eliezer disagree: Elazar ben Shammua and Eliezer ben Hyrcanus. Likewise Yevamot, chapter 3; see Responsa Chut Hashani, section 18.

(c) His father Hyrcanus was very wealthy. See Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, chapters 1–2, how he began learning at twenty-eight. Bereshit Rabbah, beginning of section 42: Eliezer ben Hyrcanus’s brothers plowed the plain; he plowed the mountain. His cow fell and broke. “For my good my cow broke,” he said, and fled to Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai. He ate clods of earth until his mouth smelled foul. They told Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, “Eliezer’s breath is unbearable.” He replied, “As your mouth became foul for Torah, so your learning’s fragrance will go from one end of the world to the other.” Later his father came to disinherit him. (Rashi: his brothers accused him before their father: “He abandoned you in old age, yet after your death will share equally with us.” He came to Jerusalem to obtain Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai’s agreement to disinherit him.) He found him expounding, with the province’s great men seated before him: ben Tzitzit Hakkeset, Nakdimon ben Guryon, and ben Kalba Savua; he found him expounding, etc. His father said, “My son, I came only to disinherit you. Now all my property is yours as a gift.” He replied, “It is forbidden to me; I shall have only my brothers’ equal share.” Avot de-Rabbi Natan, chapter 6: he was twenty-two and had not studied Torah. Once he said, “I shall study before Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.” His father Hyrcanus said, “You shall not taste food until you plow a full furrow.” He rose early and plowed it. They say it was the eve of Shabbat; he went and ate at his father-in-law’s. Some say he tasted nothing from the sixth hour on Friday to the sixth hour after Shabbat. On the road he saw a stone resembling [something unstated], took it and put it in his mouth; some say it was cattle dung. He lodged at his inn and sat before Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai in Jerusalem until his mouth smelled foul. “Eliezer, my son, have you eaten today?” He was silent. Again he asked; silence. He summoned his hosts: “Has Eliezer eaten with you?” “We thought perhaps he ate with the master.” “I thought he ate with you. Between us we have lost Eliezer,” etc. “As foul breath came from your mouth, so a good name in Torah shall come.” Hyrcanus heard he studied with Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai: “I shall exclude Eliezer from my property by a vow.” That day Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai was expounding. Hearing he had come, he posted guards: “If he comes to sit, do not let him.” They refused him a seat; he skipped and climbed until reaching bar Tzitzit Hakkeset, etc., sitting among them trembling. Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai looked at Eliezer: “Open your mouth and expound.” “I cannot begin.” He and the students pressed him; he stood and expounded things no ear had heard. For every utterance Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai rose and kissed his head. Hyrcanus said, “I came only to exclude,” etc., as above in the Midrash.

(d) Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai was his teacher, Chagigah 3b: Rabbi Eliezer said, “Thus I received from Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.” Sukkah 28a: his student. Beitzah 5, beginning of b: Eliezer’s students told him, “Your colleagues have already voted against you,” including Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai. Rosh Hashanah 31b: though he was his student, they said “your colleagues,” because as students it was improper to tell their master “your teacher”; see there. He called him a plastered cistern, Avot de-Rabbi Natan, chapter 14; Avot, chapter 2. Rabbi Eliezer went to see his teacher Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai on the new moon. Rabban Yochanan addressed him as a well of water clear of dross and asked, “What do you need of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai?” He replied, “One must greet one’s teacher,” Zohar.

(e) Tosafot, Shabbat 104a, “Children came to the study hall,” etc.: Jerusalem Talmud, Megillah, chapter 1, halakhah 11, and Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 1, say Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua were among those children, differing from our Talmud, which places them in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s days. Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer’s statement that he did not learn until grown means he did not engage in study until grown. End quotation. (Pi Shenayim, entry mantzepakh: Shabbat says the seers instituted the final-letter forms; Megillah, that they were forgotten and reestablished. Jerusalem Talmud: the seers were the children. Temurah: three thousand laws were forgotten during mourning for Moses; they asked Joshua to restore them, but he did not. Thus Shabbat’s children said something not said “in Joshua’s days” specifically: he did not restore what was forgotten, and these children did.) “Justice, justice shall you pursue”: follow Rabbi Eliezer to Lod, Sanhedrin, chapter 4, 32b. He was “Sinai,” while Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh uprooted mountains; see Asarah Ma'amarot. A student, Rabbi Yehudah ben Gurya (see there), ruled before him. He told his wife Imma Shalom that the student would not survive the year; thus it was, Eruvin 63a. Jerusalem Talmud, Gittin, chapter 1, halakhah 2, and Shevi'it, chapter 6, halakhah 1: he would not survive the week; likewise Sifra, Shemini. His sons were very handsome because of restraint in intercourse, Nedarim 20, beginning of b. His face shone when expounding, as “Moses’ face is like the sun,” etc. Midrash Chazit, “For the fragrance of your oils”: Rabbi Yehoshua kissed the stone Eliezer sat on: “The stone resembles Sinai; its sitter, the Ark of the Covenant.” No one preceded him to the study hall, etc.; Men of the Great Assembly, Hillel, etc., and Eliezer, etc. King Agrippa’s steward asked him, Sukkah 27a. Avodah Zarah 16b: he was arrested for heresy because he heard heretical words and enjoyed them; see Kohelet Rabbah.

(f) He descended from Moses (Bachya in a Midrash’s name), perhaps maternally—that is, paternally he would be a Levite (likewise Asarah Ma'amarot, Chikkur Din, part II, chapter 15). See below that he was a priest. But perhaps his father’s mother descended from Moses; this is difficult. Perhaps Yuchasin means: Rabbi Eliezer was Reuben’s reincarnation, as I shall write below. Shnei Luchot Habberit, Acharei Mot, cited in K.Sh. [ק״ש; work unresolved], chapter 13, sections 3–4, says one is reincarnated only in a relative of the dead person; see at length. The paternal family is called family. Thus Eliezer descended paternally from Reuben, and from Moses through his mother. A matron asked him why the deaths for the golden calf were unequal. He replied, “A woman’s wisdom is only in the spindle,” Yoma 66b. His son Hyrcanus said, “For not answering one Torah matter, you have lost three hundred kor of tithe from her each year.” “Let them burn, rather than give words of Torah to women,” he replied. Jerusalem Talmud, Sotah, chapter 3, halakhah 4; Tosafot, Sotah 21b; Bamidbar Rabbah, section 9. Yedei Moshe: “Eliezer ben Hyrcanus was a priest; since he refused to answer, she did not give him tithes.” End quotation. Very puzzling: why did Maimonides and Yuchasin not list him among priests? See the chronological section under Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok. Moreover, did a matron give tithe?

(g) He lived at the second Temple’s destruction: he and Rabbi Yehoshua carried Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai’s bier, Gittin 56a; Tosafot, Nazir 33b. At Rabban Gamliel the elder’s death, Rabbi Eliezer was old; see there. He saw the death of Gamliel’s grandson, his own brother-in-law (see Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh). Avot de-Rabbi Natan, chapter 16: he raised his sister’s daughter, sharing his bed for thirteen years, and betrothed her in his old age.

(h) Rabbi Akiva was his student. Tosefta, Sanhedrin, chapter 10: Akiva said, “Eliezer expounded three hundred laws about a sorceress; I learned only two,” Sanhedrin 68a. “Akiva, am I thus in your eyes?”, Bava Kamma 41b. He said only what he heard from his teacher, Sukkah 27b; Yoma 66b. Eliezer decreed forty fasts, but rain did not come. Akiva said, “Who makes the wind blow,” etc., and rain came. Akiva appeased him with a parable, etc., Zohar, Shemot, II 15a [Heilprin prints עכ״ד]. Eliezer saw in a dream the verse “Do not pray for this people.”

(i) Bava Metzia 59, beginning of b: an oven made in sections, cut into rings with sand between them—Eliezer declares it pure, the sages impure. It is taught: that day Eliezer gave every answer in the world, but they did not accept them. “If the law follows me, let this carob prove it.” It uprooted itself a hundred cubits; some say four hundred. “No proof from a carob,” they replied. “Let the water channel prove it.” It flowed backward. “No proof from a water channel.” “Let the study hall’s walls prove it.” They leaned to fall. Rabbi Yehoshua rebuked them: “If scholars contend in law, what business have you?” They did not fall out of respect for Yehoshua, or straighten out of respect for Eliezer, and still stand leaning. “Let heaven prove it.” A heavenly voice: “What have you against Eliezer? The law follows him everywhere.” Yehoshua stood: “It is not in heaven.” Torah was already given at Sinai; we disregard a heavenly voice, since You wrote, “Follow the majority.” Rabbi Natan met Elijah: “What did the Holy One do then?” “He smiled: ‘My children have defeated Me; My children have defeated Me.’” That day they brought everything Eliezer had declared pure and burned it, voted regarding him, and “blessed” him [a euphemism for excommunication]. “Who will inform him?” Akiva said, “I shall, lest someone unsuitable tell him and destroy the whole world.” Dressed and wrapped in black, he sat four cubits away. “Akiva, why is today different?” “My teacher, it seems your colleagues separate themselves from you.” He tore his clothes, removed his shoes, slipped down to the ground, and wept. The world was struck: a third of olives, a third of wheat, a third of barley. Some say even dough in a woman’s hands swelled. It is taught: great wrath that day—wherever Eliezer looked burned. Rabban Gamliel too was in a ship; a wave threatened to drown him. “Surely this is because of Eliezer. Master of the world, You know I acted neither for my honor nor my father’s house, but for Yours, that disputes not multiply in Israel.” The sea calmed. Imma Shalom, Eliezer’s wife, sister of Rabban Gamliel the nasi, Shabbat 116a, henceforth prevented him falling on his face in prayer. Once a poor man came; she brought out bread and found him fallen on his face. “Rise—you have killed my brother.” Just then the horn sounded from Gamliel’s house announcing his death; see there. Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Megallechin, differs somewhat; see there.

(j) R.Ch. [ר״ח; authority unresolved] writes: why appoint his student Elazar ben Azaryah nasi instead of Eliezer? Because he was old, and an old man is not appointed to the Sanhedrin (see Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai). Jerusalem Talmud, end of Sotah: a heavenly voice in Yavneh’s upper room said two were fit for the holy spirit, one being Shmuel the small, who died in Gamliel the elder’s lifetime. Gamliel the elder died eighteen years before the destruction. They looked to Eliezer ben Hyrcanus as fit for the Divine Presence. Surely this was after much study; he began at twenty-one or twenty-two. Shmuel the small may have died years before Gamliel the elder; thus Eliezer was old when Elazar ben Azaryah was appointed. Alternatively, he was separated from the sages; or Gamliel’s disputant; or of Shammai’s house, hence called shammuti. Rashi, Shabbat 130b, citing Jerusalem Talmud, end of Happiggam; Niddah 7b; Jerusalem Talmud, Shevi'it, chapter 9; apparently Jerusalem Talmud, Beitzah, chapter 1, halakhah 4; Tosafot, Beitzah 35a; Jerusalem Talmud, Terumot, Se'ah Terumah; Arukh, entry shamet. Etz Chayyim [ע״ח; reading provisional], Darkhei Hammishnah: “Though Eliezer’s teacher Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai was Hillel’s student, perhaps afterward he returned and served Shammai.” End quotation. Responsa Ben Ze'ev, at דשמ״ג [locator retained]: the Talmud’s authors knew all Eliezer’s opinions followed Beit Shammai; see there, and דמ״ו. Responsa Chavvot Yair: “Then Tarfon too was Beit Shammai’s student, as were several others; should we not rule like them? Requires examination.” End quotation. Beitzah 34, Mishnah, “Eliezer further said”: see Rashi and Tosafot. The law follows him in divorce documents, Gittin 4a; Rashi: in this matter; see 86b. Shmuel says the law follows Eliezer in four matters, Niddah 7b. Chavvot Yair: “I think this means: although shammuti, of Beit Shammai, the law follows the rulings he gave before that incident,” there in his omissions. Requires examination: according to Rashi, that he was “blessed,” why should this count against him? Even a rebellious elder who says something sound—why not rule like him? See my lengthy discussion in the rules.

(k) When ill, four elders came: Tarfon, Yose the Galilean, Elazar ben Azaryah, and Akiva. Because of excommunication they sat four cubits away. It was Friday; his son Hyrcanus wanted to remove his father’s tefillin, Shabbat approaching, etc. They told him, “You are better for Israel than sun, rain, father, and mother.” At death he said Akiva would die an unusual death, end of Dinei Mamonot 68; “Fierce wrath is in the world,” there 101. See Midrash Hanne'elam, Zohar, beginning of Vayera, at length. Before dying: “Clear the house because of impurity; give a chair to Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai”; some say Hezekiah, king of Judah, as his teacher Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai had instructed, Jerusalem Talmud, Avodah Zarah, chapter 3, halakhah 1, and end of Sotah. His soul departed answering their question: “Pure,” end of Dinei Mamonot. He died Friday at twilight; after Shabbat they carried his bier from Caesarea to Lod. Akiva met it, striking his flesh until blood flowed to the ground, and expounded: “My father, my father, Israel’s chariot and horsemen,” there. Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat, chapter 2, halakhah 7, differs somewhat: Yehoshua entered and removed his tefillin, embracing, kissing, and weeping: “My teacher, the vow is released! My teacher, Israel’s chariot and horsemen!” His burial is at Kefar Alma; see Elazar ben Arakh, Gelilot Eretz Yisrael. In Yavneh is Eliezer the great’s study hall, same work. Lev Aryeh, Chukkat: he was Reuben’s reincarnation, saved on arrest for heresy since Reuben was righteous in Joseph’s sale. Thus Leah’s “For the Lord saw [רא״ה] my affliction” gives the initials Rabbi Eliezer Haggadol. End quotation. Corresponding to this, Responsa Halakhot Ketannot: “My strength and first of my vigor” has the numerical value “This is Rabbi Eliezer ben Hyrcanus,” including the total [ע״ה; reading provisional]. That phrase concerns Reuben; understand. G.N. [ג״נ; work unresolved]: when Moses ascended on high, he heard the Holy One state a law in Eliezer’s name, prayed he be his descendant, and prayed he be saved when arrested, as above, as he said of his son Elazar, “My father’s God was my help.” End quotation; see Asarah Ma'amarot. See Elazar ben Perata: Reuben’s reincarnation, saved on arrest for heresy, Avodah Zarah, chapter 1; see there.

(l) Onkelos the convert received from him. Acherim say in Eliezer’s name, Beitzah 4. Rabbi Elazar in Rabbi Eliezer’s name (see there). Rabbi Ilai the elder, his student; Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah, his student. Rabbi Berekhiah son of Rabbi Abba bar Kahana in his name. His brother Dosa ben Hyrcanus—requires examination. Rabbi Dostai son of Rabbi Yannai in his name; Rabbi Chananya ben Teradyon in his name; Abba Chanan in his name. Rabbi Yehudah ben Gudgeda; Rabbi Yehudah ben Gadish testified before him; Rabbi Yehudah, his student’s student; Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hyrcanus, perhaps his brother; Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai, his teacher. Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri in his name; Rabbi Yose of Dormaskit, his student; Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Yehudah in his name—requires examination. Rabbi Yose ben Perata, his student; Rabbi Yose ben Peridi; Rabbi Yose ben Kippur in his name; Rabbi Matya ben Charash, his student. Rabbi Nechunya ben Elnatan disputes with him. Rabbi Tzadok; Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar in his name.
